sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in West Orange?
sections.html:
West Orange is an Essex County suburb on the slopes of the Watchung Mountains, and every residential sale needs a Certificate of Continued Occupancy from the township before the deed changes hands. The rest of the process is familiar: a contract, title work, a closing, and a deed recorded with the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages.

The township is about five miles west of downtown Newark and 12 miles west of Manhattan, which is why buyers here weigh commute times and hillside streets about as much as school names.

sections.h2: What do West Orange's population and housing numbers show?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 48,843 residents in 2020, up from 46,207 in 2010, and estimates 49,557 for July 2025. The township covers 12.00 square miles of land, or about 4,069 people per square mile.

sections.h2: How do West Orange's four neighborhoods and history affect value?
sections.html:
West Orange was part of Newark, then Orange Township, before it separated and was incorporated as a township on April 10, 1863. It became a town in 1900 and switched back to a township in 1980 to qualify for a larger share of federal revenue sharing. The local landmarks are Thomas Edison's laboratory, now a national historical park on Main Street, and Llewellyn Park, laid out in the 1850s as one of the first planned residential communities in the country.

  • Downtown West Orange and the Valley lie in the low basin along the border with Orange and Montclair. This is the densest and oldest part, with the municipal building, police headquarters and the library nearby.
  • The First Mountain climbs along Northfield, Mount Pleasant and Eagle Rock Avenues, with Victorian, Tudor and mid-century houses, estates, and views of the Newark and Manhattan skylines. Hutton Park, Gregory and Llewellyn Park sit here.
  • Pleasant Valley and Pleasantdale hold postwar suburban streets and a walkable business district.
  • The Second Mountain borders South Mountain Reservation and resembles neighboring Millburn and Livingston.

South Mountain Reservation and the 400-acre Eagle Rock Reservation frame the township, and the Essex Green Shopping Center, at 350,000 square feet, is the largest outdoor mall in the county.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools matter to West Orange buyers?
sections.html:
Interstate 280 crosses the township east to west, Route 10 runs through the western area, and County Routes 577 and 508 carry local traffic. West Orange maintains 89.63 of its roughly 114.5 miles of road, with the county and state handling the rest. NJ Transit buses 21, 29, 71, 73 and 79 reach Newark, route 101 goes to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and a weekday township jitney connects to the Brick Church, Orange and South Orange train stations.

West Orange Public Schools run 12 schools from prekindergarten through West Orange High School, which had 2,098 students in 2019-20. Private options include Seton Hall Preparatory School and Golda Och Academy. Buyers often ask which elementary school serves a given street, so check zoning with the district before you advertise it.

sections.h2: What is a Certificate of Continued Occupancy in West Orange?
sections.html:
A Certificate of Continued Occupancy, or CCO, is the township's proof that a residential building meets health, safety, fire and land use rules at the time of a sale or rental. Under Chapter 25 of the township code, the owner of record must obtain it before selling any residential structure with one unit or more, and the Construction Official issues it.

  • The fee is set by resolution of the Township Council, so ask the office for the current amount. The township's form says there are no refunds once an application is processed.
  • Questions go to 973-325-4111 or planning@westorange.org, the contacts printed on the township's residential application, which asks for the seller, buyer, closing date and any minor children who will live in the home.
  • The tax assessor must tell people requesting tax searches that a CCO is required for the sale.
  • Minor violations may earn a temporary CCO of up to 30 days, and the permanent certificate then carries no additional fee.
  • Anyone who closes without a CCO stays liable, and the owner faces a separate violation for each day until one issues. Real estate agents and attorneys who take part in the deal may also be held responsible.

If you believe no CCO is needed, you can ask the Construction Official for a written determination for a $25 fee.

sections.h2: How do West Orange property taxes and appeals work?
sections.html:
New Jersey sets assessment appeals to run through the county board of taxation, and for West Orange that is the Essex County Board. The regular deadline is April 1 of the tax year, or 45 days after the township mails assessment notices if that is later. Appeals above $1 million in assessed value can go straight to the State Tax Court.

Because the assessor must flag the CCO whenever someone requests a tax search, expect the title company to contact the township early in your sale. Ask the assessor and tax collector for your current balance, any open sewer charges and the status of the quarter so the closing statement is exact.

sections.h2: Where is a West Orange deed recorded and what does the seller pay?
sections.html:
West Orange deeds go to the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which records property transactions for all 22 municipalities in the county and holds deeds and mortgages going back to 1637. The state realty transfer fee is charged to the seller when the deed is recorded. For a sale over $350,000, the slice between $550,000 and $850,000 is charged at $5.30 per $500, and a sale above $1 million adds a Graduated Percent Fee of 1 percent or more.

The median home value of $557,300 sits close to the $550,000 break, so an average West Orange sale falls near the point where the rate steps up. Your attorney will calculate the fee on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a West Orange house?
sections.html:
Owners here usually choose a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or a cash offer.

  • A listing exposes a mountain-view or Llewellyn Park-area house to the full buyer pool and is the usual path for a house in good condition.
  • A private sale saves a commission but needs a lawyer for the contract and the CCO paperwork.
  • A cash buyer fits a house that needs work, a multi-unit building with tenants, or an estate where heirs want to close quickly.

In every case the CCO inspection is a requirement of the sale. Ask any buyer who pays for corrections and get it in the contract.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Continued Occupancy to sell my West Orange house?
faqs.a: Yes. West Orange's land use code requires a CCO before the sale or rental of any existing residential structure with one unit or more. The owner of record applies and the Construction Official issues it.

faqs.q: How much does a West Orange CCO cost?
faqs.a: The Township Council sets the fee by resolution, so the amount changes. Call 973-325-4111 to confirm it, and note that the township does not refund an application once it has been processed.

faqs.q: What if my West Orange house fails the CCO inspection?
faqs.a: For minor violations the Construction Official may issue a temporary CCO for up to 30 days. A permanent certificate issued after the repairs carries no additional fee.

faqs.q: Where does the deed for a West Orange sale get recorded?
faqs.a: The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records it, along with the seller's realty transfer fee. Your closing attorney or title company normally files it for you.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my West Orange property tax assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the Essex County Board of Taxation by April 1 of the tax year, or within 45 days of the notice mailing if that is later. Assessments above $1 million can go to the State Tax Court.
